newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki nudges ahead on firmer Nokia.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki nudges ahead on firmer Nokia.

text.p: Shares were mixed with the thinly traded market inching forward on Monday on firmer Nokia, while profit-taking hit Raisio and Huhtamaki and Kesko slipped after news of TukoSpar demerger plans, brokers said.
The HEX index edged up 0.11 percent to 2238.66, with advancers leading decliners 37 to 33 and 27 unchanged. Volume was 296 million markka.

Nokia rose 2.00 markka to 215.50 in fairly lively trade, tracking bullishness in Swedish rival Ericsson ahead of Ericsson's nine-month results due on Tuesday. Nokia accounted for 39 percent of bourse volume.
"We may have a volatile market tomorrow due to Ericsson," one broker said, noting that the two telecom majors tend to move in tandem.

Food and feed group Raisio fell 6.00 markka to 304.00 in lively 19 million markka trade, and confectionery and packaging group Huhtamaki lost 5.50 markka to 199.50, with investors cashing in on recent gains, brokers said.
Retail and wholesale group Kesko dropped 2.00 markka in fair trade to end at 72.50 after announcing plans to sell some 40 percent of its Tuko acquisition in order to satisfy EU competition watchdogs.
"The plan, if carried out, cuts some of the upside seen in Kesko stock," one broker said. But there was also buying interest in Kesko, brokers said.
